titel: Your entry into the chess book

unterschrift.text: The starting position. White is at the bottom and moves first.

abbildungen.unterabschnitt: The coordinate system: every square has a name

unterschrift.text: The empty board: files a–h from left to right, ranks 1–8 from bottom to top. White is at the bottom, Black at the top. Gray: the e-file and the 4th rank. Where they cross lies e4 (gold). The second gold square is a8, the top left corner.
King d4. Gold: its target squares. Red: e3, e4 and e5 – the black rook on e8 attacks them (gray arrow), so the king may not move there.
Queen d4. It moves any distance in all eight directions and reaches 27 squares here.
Rook d4. The pawn blocks the way up. The rook may capture the black knight, but it cannot go past it to g4 and h4.
Bishop d4. It reaches 13 squares, all dark: a bishop never changes the color of its squares.
Knight d4. It reaches eight squares. Its own pawns on c4, d3, d5 and e4 (gray) do not bother it: the knight simply jumps over them.
Pawn e2. It moves straight ahead to e3 or – because it is still on its starting square – to e4 (gold). It captures the black pawns on d3 and f3 diagonally forward (red).

Checkmate. Black to move. The queen on g7 gives check (red arrow) and is protected by the king on g6, so it cannot be captured. The squares g8 and h7 (gray), where the king could escape, are attacked: the king on h8 (red) can neither escape nor capture the queen.
Stalemate. Black to move. The same material, but the queen stands on f7: the king on h8 (red) is
in check, yet g8, g7 and h7 (gray) are attacked. Black has no legal move – the game is a draw.
Before White castles kingside, White to move. Gold: the paths of king and rook. Gray: f1 and g1 must be empty and not attacked.
After castling, Black to move. Gold: the king stands on g1, the rook on f1.

Before White castles queenside, White to move. Gold: the paths of king and rook. Gray: d1 and c1 must be empty and not attacked. b1 only has to be empty: the bishop on e4 attacks that square (red arrow), yet castling is allowed.
After castling queenside, Black to move. Gold: the king stands on c1, the rook on d1.
Black to move. The pawn on d7 can move two squares to d5 (gold arrow); White has a pawn on e5.

The black pawn has moved to d5, White to move. The square d6 marked in red is the target square of the en passant capture – White may now immediately capture there with the pawn on e5 (gold arrow), even though no piece stands there. The pawn on d5 (gray) is removed from the board.
After the en passant capture, Black to move. The white pawn stands on d6; the black pawn on d5 (gray square) has been removed.
The white pawn on a7 reaches the last rank with its next move (gold arrow).
After promotion, Black to move. On a8 the pawn has immediately become a queen and gives check along the eighth rank (red arrow).

loesung.text: Move 1: White moves the pawn to e4, Black to e5. Move 2: White moves the knight to f3, Black to c6. Move 3: White moves the bishop to c4, Black to c5. Remember: the letter names the piece, the square after it its destination, and a pawn move has no letter.

erklaerung.text: Each pair of moves consists of a white move and a black move: pawns to e4 and e5, knights to f3 and c6, bishops to c4 and c5. The capital letter names the piece, the square after it its destination; a pawn move has no letter.

Write down the next three half-moves with move numbers: Black moves the pawn from h7 to h6, the white bishop captures the knight on f6, and the black queen recaptures. After that, White wants to move the knight from b1 to d2. Why is the notation

loesung.text: . Since the line begins with a black move, three dots follow the move number, and both captures carry an x. Besides the knight on b1, the knight on f3 can also move to d2, so the notation has to say which one is meant:
. Remember: if two identical pieces can move to the same square, you also give the file the piece comes from, and if the file is the same, the rank.

erklaerung.text: A black move at the start of a line gets three dots after the number, a capture gets an x. Because both knights could move to d2, the move is written 8. Nbd2: the b-file says which knight is meant.

aufgabe.text: The three positions A, B and C arise one after another from the starting position (
). Write down the move sequence that leads to them, with move numbers, in algebraic notation. Pay particular attention to how a pawn capture is written.

loesung.text: . Position A arises after the first pair of moves: both sides have advanced a pawn two squares. In position B, the white pawn has captured on d5 from the e-file. The move is therefore written
. In position C, the black queen has recaptured on d5 (
), and this opening is called the Scandinavian Defense. Remember: when a pawn captures, the file it comes from stands before the x.

erklaerung.text: The positions arise from 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5, the Scandinavian Defense. When a pawn captures, the file it comes from stands before the x: 2. exd5, not 2. xd5.
